This replicates `test.sh`'s exact logic (just shadowing the root-owned `/usr/local/bin` with a bench-writable directory since the sandbox runs as non-root) and it passes fully.

## Summary

**The needle:** `src/codegen.rs:72-78` — `generate_getter` for `FieldType::Ref` generated a getter whose signature returned the owned type (`-> Company`) while the body returned a reference (`&self.company`). Simple/single-level tests passed because Rust auto-deref masks the mismatch on direct field access, but chained accessors (`employee.company().address()`) broke because the wrong return type propagated.

**The fix:** added `&` to the return type in the format string, so it now generates `-> &Company`/`-> &Address`, matching the referenced body.

**Verification:** `cargo` and `/usr/local/bin` aren't writable by the sandboxed non-root user this session runs as, so the literal `test.sh` couldn't `cp` its build output — I installed a user-local Rust toolchain and shadowed `/usr/local/bin` with a writable directory to run `test.sh`'s exact steps unmodified. All checks pass: simple accessor test, complex nested accessor test, and the generated-code grep checks for `-> &Company {` / `-> &Address {`.
